Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: ACTION: Reroute steps & post-incident follow-up — US + APAC edge outage

Hi Sandeep / AetherPay Ops team,

Quick update: our telemetry shows degraded connectivity for a subset of our US-East and APAC edge aggregator nodes between 08:40–09:05 UTC. Traffic routed through those nodes experienced increased latency and token errors; the core model pools remained healthy. We've implemented an automated traffic cutover that prefers EU-central pools for affected customers, but that only applies when a region override is enabled or the SDK's region fallback is configured.

Immediate ask: please apply the temporary region override below so your traffic flows to the EU pools until we confirm regional stabilization. This is a non-breaking change and can be reverted once we say the incident is closed.

Steps (recommended order):
1) SDK customers: set REDWOOD_REGION_OVERRIDE=eu-central in your staging canary first, then prod if healthy.
2) HTTP clients: add header X-Redwood-Region: eu-central to requests.
3) If you use a fixed hostname, switch from api-us.redwood.ai to api-eu.redwood.ai for the duration.

We do not expect token or data re-ingestion; sessions and KV caches remain intact. We will not bill for any emergency reroute-related quota overages during the mitigation window.

Attachments: reroute-playbook.pdf (short checklist), curl-examples.txt (sample headers/commands).

I will follow up with a short timeline and post-incident summary once we've validated recovery. Please reply here when the override is set so we can monitor traffic.

Ben Carter
Accounts — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Sandeep — thanks for the quick canary. Short answers:
1) In-flight requests: If an upstream request timed out, clients should receive a 5xx and the SDK will surface a retryable error; it won't be replayed automatically unless you have client-side retry enabled. Our suggestion: for critical ingestion paths enable conservative retries (2 attempts, exponential backoff) in the next 30m while the cutover completes.
2) Tokens & TTL: no change to token signature validation or TTL; session tokens remain valid. The region override is routing-only.

Procurement note: we will log the incident window and set a credit for any emergency burst usage caused by the reroute — I'll loop in Billing if you need a formal invoice note.

For convenience, here are the curl examples (also attached as curl-examples.txt):

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central" https://api-eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate

I'll monitor traffic and confirm when the edge cluster is healthy.

Ben

Subject: Post-incident: concise timeline & next steps for AetherPay (US/APAC edge event)

Hi Sandeep — following up with a brief post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for confirming the region override on July 23rd; our monitoring shows AetherPay traffic was successfully served from EU pools between 09:25–12:40 UTC while we repaired the affected aggregators.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 08:39: alerted: edge aggregator error spike in us-east + apac-east zones.
- 08:45: mitigation: traffic steering rule enacted to prefer eu-central for affected customers.
- 09:25: AetherPay applied X-Redwood-Region: eu-central (canary).
- 09:30–12:40: steady-state in EU pools; reduced errors and latency normalized.
- 12:43: Region nodes drained and validated; automated routing restored to normal preference.

What we are sharing: a short postmortem PDF (attached) with the root cause, mitigation steps, and our preventive actions (improved aggregator circuit breaker and faster failover). We also added a monitoring alert specifically for the cross-region routing backpressure we observed.

Action items for AetherPay:
- Confirm that you saw no data loss for the ingestion window (we have logs showing successful deliveries once rerouted).
- Let us know if you want a refundable credit note recorded against the July usage for the mitigation window — Ben can coordinate the billing entry.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute review with our reliability team to walk through the postmortem and recommended SDK hardening (retries/backoff).

Thanks again for fast coordination. If everything looks good I'll mark this ticket closed on July 30th unless you request otherwise.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success
Redwood Inference
